comparison_intro: One behavior contract, three implementations. Run the companion files and the same three acceptance tests against shared fixture data.

language_notes.sas: SAS MEAN excludes numeric missing; an all-missing row remains missing. Loader maps __MISSING__ to SAS . before translation.
language_notes.python: pandas mean(axis=1, skipna=True) averages across named inputs; all-missing rows yield NaN. Loader decodes the numeric sentinel.
language_notes.r: Base R rowMeans(..., na.rm=TRUE) returns NaN for an all-missing row; normalize it to NA_real_. Both are detected by is.na().

semantic_notes.title: Missing is not zero
semantic_notes.text: The denominator is the number of observed values. A row with only one observed zero returns zero, while an all-missing row stays missing.

semantic_notes.title: Preserve the inputs
semantic_notes.text: The translation adds average to a new table. It retains x, y, z, row identifiers and row order, including their missing positions.

tests.name: Original three-row fixture
tests.input: Complete, partly missing and all-missing rows from the original example.
tests.catches: Wrong axis, propagating one missing input, or replacing all-missing with zero.

tests.name: Added single-observation boundary
tests.input: Added validation rows [0, missing, missing] and [missing, -6, missing].
tests.catches: Dividing by three, treating zero as missing, or excluding negative values.

tests.name: Preservation, numeric type and order
tests.input: All shared rows in reverse order; non-default Python index.
tests.expected: Original input values/missing masks retained; row order retained; average numeric.
tests.catches: Input mutation, row loss/reordering, index reset, or text instead of numeric results.

scope: Ordinary SAS numeric missing and finite numeric x/y/z values; no special missing codes, weights or grouping. Added edge rows are new validation examples, not new model trials.
